journeys.title: Birth of Techno
journeys.summary: From Belleville High to Berlin: how five friends from Detroit built machine music.

stops.title: The Belleville Three
stops.narration: Juan Atkins, Kevin Saunderson, and Derrick May meet at Belleville High and absorb European synth records alongside Motown and WBMX house imports.

stops.title: House arrives on the radio
stops.narration: Hot Mix 5 and the Warehouse show Detroit listeners what looped disco grooves could do to a dancefloor.

stops.title: Cybotron and Model 500
stops.narration: Atkins's sci-fi electro records sketch techno's blueprint: machines with a Black futurist voice.

stops.title: Transmat and Metroplex
stops.narration: Saunderson's KMS and May's Transmat turn Detroit bedrooms into world-class labels.

stops.title: Techno! crosses the Atlantic
stops.narration: The 1988 compilation Techno! The New Dance Sound of Detroit lands in Europe and never leaves.

vocabulary.definition: Four-on-the-floor electronic dance music pioneered in mid-1980s Detroit.

journeys.title: Kingston to London
journeys.summary: How Windrush migration carried sound-system culture across the Atlantic into UK dub, jungle, and grime.

stops.title: Yard dances
stops.narration: Open-air sound clashes make music a communal, competitive sport in Kingston.

stops.title: Windrush sound systems
stops.narration: Caribbean communities rebuild yard culture in London front rooms and blues parties.

stops.title: Dub comes home on vinyl
stops.narration: Kingston's studio innovations return as British dub records and soundsystems.

stops.title: Jungle to grime
stops.narration: Breakbeat science and Caribbean deejay vocal styles evolve into distinctly London forms.

vocabulary.definition: A crew of DJs, engineers, and MCs built around massive custom speakers.

journeys.title: Evolution of Hip-Hop
journeys.summary: From a Bronx rec room to a global lingua franca of youth culture.

stops.title: 1973: the rec room jam
stops.narration: Kool Herc's merry-go-round technique keeps b-boys dancing on the break.

stops.title: MCs step forward
stops.narration: Party shouting becomes lyricism; crews form around turntable wizards like Flash.

stops.title: Records and message
stops.narration: 'Rapper's Delight' and 'The Message' prove rap can chart and testify.

stops.title: Afrobeats dialogue
stops.narration: Nigeria's Fela-influenced pop and hip-hop trade rhythms back across the diaspora.

vocabulary.definition: The isolated drum section of a funk or soul record, looped for dancing.

furtherReading: Can't Stop Won't Stop by Jeff Chang

journeys.title: Origins of House
journeys.summary: Disco's afterlife in Black Chicago becomes the world's dance floor default.

stops.title: Disco demolition backlash
stops.narration: After Comiskey Park's anti-disco riot, queer Black clubs keep four-on-the-floor alive.

stops.title: The Warehouse
stops.narration: Frankie Knuckles edits and re-dreams disco records for a devoted midnight crowd.

stops.title: House records appear
stops.narration: Trax and DJ International press the genre's first anthems.

stops.title: Detroit listens
stops.narration: WBMX signals cross Lake Michigan; Detroit answers with its own machines.

stops.title: Acid summer
stops.narration: British ravers adopt house; 1988's Second Summer of Love begins.

vocabulary.definition: A steady kick drum on every beat, house's foundational pulse.

furtherReading: Last Night a DJ Saved My Life by Brewster & Broughton

journeys.title: Afrobeats and Diaspora
journeys.summary: Fela's afrobeat and Lagos studio culture evolve into Afrobeats, conquering charts through London.

stops.title: Afrobeat origins
stops.narration: Fela Kuti fuses highlife, funk, and Yoruba rhythm into extended protest suites.

stops.title: Studio culture matures
stops.narration: Lagos pop absorbs reggae, dancehall, hip-hop production techniques.

stops.title: London club crossover
stops.narration: Diaspora DJs build Afrobeats nights; UK charts follow.

stops.title: Global feedback loop
stops.narration: Wizkid, Burna Boy, and Tems win Grammys as Lagos-London traffic runs both ways.

vocabulary.definition: Afrobeat is Fela's 1970s genre; Afrobeats is the 2010s Nigerian/Ghanaian pop wave.

furtherReading: Fela: This Bitch of a Life by Carlos Moore
